title: test(plugin-form): pin object-form's last four member keys, closing the block (slice 11)
body:
Refs #8071 — slice 11. The card is incremental by design and stays open; 24 exemptions remain after this one.

`Clause-②: no` — test-only. Three new pin files, one promotion, one ledger edit and an empty-frontmatter changeset. No published surface moves.

## What this slice does

`object-form`'s four remaining `MEMBER_PIN_EXEMPTIONS` entries — `customFields`, `dataSource`, `mobile`, `sections` — become per-block member pins under objectui#8068's criterion, and each entry is deleted in the same change. `MEMBER_PIN_EXEMPTION_CEILING` follows 28 to 24 in the same commit. **`object-form` is the first block this card takes to zero.**

## The batch was re-taken from the CONSTANT, not from the card's prose

Taken on `origin/main` `d18322415` with a depth-aware scan of the direct property keys of `MEMBER_PIN_EXEMPTIONS` in `apps/console/src/__tests__/registry-inputs-spec-parity.test.ts`:

| reading | value |
|:--|:--|
| exemptions | 28 (ceiling reads 28, in step) |
| of which `object-form` | 4 — `customFields` · `dataSource` · `mobile` · `sections` |
| already pinned among the four | 0 |

The dispatch's reading held. The card body's enumerated key list is stale in both directions and carries a dated block saying so; this is the third slice in a row to record it.

### Set identity, checked mechanically

Keys leaving `MEMBER_PIN_EXEMPTIONS` and keys entering `MEMBER_PINS` compared as sets against the merge base:

```
exemptions      : 28 -> 24
ceiling         : 28 -> 24
pins            : 63 -> 67
LEFT exemptions : object-form.customFields, object-form.dataSource, object-form.mobile, object-form.sections
ENTERED pins    : object-form.customFields, object-form.dataSource, object-form.mobile, object-form.sections
added exemptions: []   lost pins: []
SET IDENTITY    : HOLDS      CEILING == COUNT: YES
```

## The four pins

Three are new files; `dataSource` is a promotion, grown by one row before being registered rather than credited on its strings.

**`sections`** — `packages/plugin-form/src/__tests__/objectFormSectionMembers-8071.test.tsx`. Members are section objects, pinned in the DEFAULT layout on the six keys `SimpleObjectForm`'s grouped branch reads. The row a plausible improvement breaks: `fields` is read as a SET (`sourceFields.filter(...)`), so the OBJECT's order wins and the authored member order is discarded — the opposite of the sibling key `object-form.fields`, pinned next door on authored order being PRESERVED. Also: a section resolving no field is dropped whole, heading included; `name` alone titles a section and a member with neither `name` nor `label` draws no divider; `collapsed` and `collapsible` are separate members, so `collapsed` alone renders permanently closed with no affordance.

**`customFields`** — `objectFormCustomFieldsMembers-8071.test.tsx`. Members REPLACE the metadata-generated set: the object's schema is never even fetched (`getObjectSchema` asserted at zero calls), an object field no member names is absent, and a member naming a declared field carries its OWN label. That contradicts the registration's own prose, "merged over the set generated from object metadata". The row a plausible improvement breaks is the gate's `.length > 0`: an empty array is UNAUTHORED. A fifth row pins the second read site of the same member count one layer up — `requiresDataSource` in `index.tsx` — with the identical node minus the members reporting the no-adapter panel as its control.

**`mobile`** — `objectFormMobileMembers-8071.test.tsx`. Five members are read; the registration names three by example, so `stepperFieldsPerStep` and `stickyActions` are read, change what renders, and are declared nowhere. `stepper: true` routes through the wizard unconditionally (asserted on a desktop viewport and under a raised minimum); `'auto'` needs BOTH the phone viewport and `stepperMinFields`, as three cells that each control the other two. `fullscreenLongText` is deliberately left to `ObjectForm.mobileFullscreen.test.tsx`, which owns it end to end.

**`dataSource`** — `packages/plugin-form/src/ObjectForm.elementDataSource.test.tsx`, promoted after being read end to end and grown by the row it never stated: the binding's `object` member OUTRANKS a flat `objectName` on the same node. `ElementDataSourceGate` spells it as an unconditional assignment; the friendly spelling a contributor would write is the nullish-assign one, under which a rebound form keeps editing the old object with the same fields, the same labels and no diagnostic.

## Every pin shown FAILING, and every restore proven

Four legs. Each mutates the read site toward the plausible improvement, proves the mutation reached disk before reading any result (the removed text at zero occurrences, an injected marker above zero, and the blob hash differing from HEAD's), runs the pinned file and the other three separately, then restores with `git checkout HEAD -- PATH` and proves the restore by blob hash equality plus an empty `git diff HEAD`. Every leg carried a `trap` on EXIT/INT/TERM with an absolute path.

| leg | read site mutated | mutation | pinned file | the other three |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `sections` | `ObjectForm.tsx` | resolve members in AUTHORED order | exit 1 — `1 failed / 5 passed`, row 1 named | exit 0 — 15 passed |
| `customFields` | `ObjectForm.tsx` | `hasInlineFields` read as truthiness | exit 1 — `1 failed / 4 passed`, row 4 named | exit 0 — 16 passed |
| `mobile` | `ObjectForm.tsx` | drop the undeclared `stepperFieldsPerStep` | exit 1 — `1 failed / 4 passed`, row 4 named | exit 0 — 16 passed |
| `dataSource` | `ElementDataSourceGate.tsx` | nullish-assign instead of assign | exit 1 — `1 failed / 4 passed`, the new row named | exit 0 — 16 passed |

All four restores: mutated blob differed from HEAD's, restored blob equalled HEAD's, `git diff HEAD` empty. The tests resolve these modules through the root vitest config's `resolve.alias`, which points at each package's `src` rather than its `dist`, so no rebuild sits between a mutation and the run that reads it.

## Typecheck coverage PROVEN, not assumed

`tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --noEmit --listFiles` in `packages/plugin-form` lists all four pin files (`objectFormSectionMembers-8071`, `objectFormCustomFieldsMembers-8071`, `objectFormMobileMembers-8071`, `ObjectForm.elementDataSource`) and exits 0. The first run of that probe exited 2 with real type errors in two of them, which is itself the proof the project compiles these files rather than skipping them; both errors were fixed. `tsc --noEmit --listFiles` in `apps/console` lists `registry-inputs-spec-parity.test.ts` and exits 0.

## Changeset grade MEASURED from a build

Empty frontmatter. Both packages were built, and the corpus scanned is what each `package.json` `files[]` actually ships.

| package | absent controls | lit controls |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `@object-ui/plugin-form` | the three new test-file basenames and the shared describe-string fragment: 0 files each | `ObjectForm` 21, `mobileStickyActions` 4, `stepperFieldsPerStep` 4 |
| `@object-ui/console` | `MEMBER_PINS`, `MEMBER_PIN_EXEMPTIONS`, `MEMBER_PIN_EXEMPTION_CEILING`, `AWAITING_A_PIN`: 0 files each | `ObjectStack` 22, `console` 102 |

`node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` exits 0 and prints that every declared changeset has an empty frontmatter, "which is the explicit exemption and a complete answer to this gate". `check-changeset-no-major` exits 0.

The changeset probe itself is whitespace-tolerant, because changeset prose wraps near eighty columns and a line-anchored `grep -F` is structurally blind to it: two lit controls that each span a wrap read HIT under the normalising probe and the same phrase reads 0 under `grep -cF`, with an absent control reading MISS.

## Verification

Exit codes captured to disk before any pipe, in every case.

- `apps/console/src/__tests__/registry-inputs-spec-parity.test.ts` — exit 0, 199 passed.
- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/plugin-form/` — exit 0, 96 files, 919 passed / 1 skipped.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/console test` — exit 0, 101 files, 1158 passed.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-form type-check` and `pnpm --filter @object-ui/console type-check` — both exit 0.
- Gates, all exit 0: `check:control-bytes`, `check:new-line-citations`, `check:test-path-roots`, `check:vi-mock-specifiers`, `check:vi-mock-inherit`, `check:vi-mock-override-shape`, `check:changeset-claims`, `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check:sdui-registration-pins`, `check:unreferenced-sources`, plus both changeset scripts. The changeset family and `check:new-line-citations` were re-run at the final head `94c7b66eb`.
- Lint, narrowed and declared: `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-form --filter @object-ui/console lint` — exit 0, 0 errors. Those two packages are exactly the packages this diff touches files in. A targeted `eslint --no-inline-config --format json` over the five changed files linted 5 files with 0 errors and 12 warnings, all `@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any`, the same warning the neighbouring pin files carry. The narrowing is safe because this repo's `eslint.config.js` extends `tseslint.configs.recommended` and declares no `project` / `projectService` / `tsconfigRootDir` (grep for those four tokens: 0, with `tseslint.configs.recommended` reading 1 as the lit control) — linting is not type-aware, so this diff cannot move the verdict on any file it does not contain.
- Control-character self-scan over every changed file beyond the gate: no hits.
- Governed surface: `node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` over all six paths prints NOT GOVERNED.
- Serial constraint re-taken over the open-PR 全集 immediately before the first write and again before the push: intersection EMPTY both times.

## Findings handed back, ⛔ not filed and ⛔ not fixed here

1. **`customFields` is documented as merging and REPLACES.** The per-member merge exists as code — `schema.customFields?.find((f) => f.name === name)` in the metadata branch — and is unreachable, because that branch runs only when the key is absent or empty, so the lookup is always over nothing. Either the prose or the code is wrong; which one is a contract question.
2. **The default layout drops a section's `description`.** `SectionDivider` renders one and the five rebuild arms (`tabbed` / `wizard` / `split` / `drawer` / `modal`) all copy it; the default grouped branch does not, so the same authored member renders in five layouts and vanishes in the sixth. Pinned as behaviour with the section's own `label` in the same call as the live control.
3. **A section declared `collapsed` without `collapsible` is unopenable.** The toggle is installed only when `collapsible` is set, while the initial state reads `collapsed` regardless — so the fields are hidden with no affordance and nothing declared warns the author.

Both 1 and 2 are pinned on CURRENT behaviour, so whichever way each is settled the pin goes red and has to be re-read. That is deliberate.
